brief: A seven-cell honeycomb work surface, covered on top, with every open outside edge finished with caps.

requirements.requirement: Seven-cell honeycomb work surface (centre cell plus six surrounding cells)
requirements.evidence: Seven Hex base · Full pieces at axial (0,0), (1,0), (1,-1), (0,-1), (-1,0), (-1,1), (0,1) on level 0, forming a flower/honeycomb of seven cells. check_build: no issues, meshClash clear.
Seven full top covers (cover:-1,0 / -1,1 / 0,-1 / 0,0 / 0,1 / 1,-1 / 1,0; face top), one over every cell.

requirements.requirement: Every open outside edge finished with caps
requirements.evidence: capOpenFaces added 18 solid end caps on the perimeter faces of the outer cells; lockJoints added 12 joint bolts joining the cells. The configurator reported no warnings.

finish.summary: Built a seven-cell honeycomb work surface: seven full hex bases, each with a top cover, the perimeter open faces closed with 18 solid caps, and the joints bolted. check_build reports no issues and a clear mesh check. The look tool did not show the surface from above, so I verified it through the build data rather than a rendered view. No props were added since the brief did not ask for them.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
